findings.passage: “Gun violence is one of the most serious issues facing our country today, and the best way to prevent felons from obtaining firearms is to be proactive about having universal background checks on firearm sales.
findings.note: Press release from his office after the Assembly passed AB 58 (mandatory minimum sentences for felons who illegally possess a firearm). The release says he voted for a minority-caucus amendment to add background checks on firearm purchases; it continues that the bills passed should have included a requirement to run background checks on firearm sales.
subjects: universal background checks on firearm sales

findings.motion: Minority-caucus amendment to AB 58 adding background checks on firearm purchases
findings.note: His office's release says he voted in favor of this amendment to AB 58 (as written by his own office; the roll call itself was not opened).

findings.passage: After the distressing active shooter incident in 2018, we should all feel a great urgency to prevent such an event from ever reoccurring. Active shooter incidents like this one have already impacted many communities across the state and it is our duty as legislators to protect Wisconsin from the threat posed by undetectable firearms.
findings.note: His quoted statement in the release announcing a bill with Senator Hesselbein to close the ghost gun loophole (firearms without serial numbers and undetectable firearms).

findings.passage: Ensuring that people can be free from gun violence, regardless of where they live, work, and play remains a top priority of ours. Implementing a gun buyback program in Wisconsin provides citizens with an opportunity to voluntarily dispose of unwanted firearms.
findings.note: Joint statement of Senator Agard and Joers on introducing a bill to create a voluntary gun buyback program; the statement is shared, not his alone.
